**Item 1.**  `R_qd(E)` is an ideal.  If nonzero, it is projection-generated by
hypothesis, and all quotients are UCT.  The radical theorem forbids this, so
`R_qd(E) = 0`.

Special cases.
- With finitely many ideals, every quotient has a finite composition series
  whose simple subquotients are subquotients of `E`.  So it is UCT by
  two-out-of-three for nuclear extensions.
- In real rank zero every ideal is generated by its projections.  With finitely
  many ideals, finitely many projections `p_1, ..., p_k` generate, and so does
  `p_1 ⊕ ... ⊕ p_k`.

**Item 2.**  `E/(K⊗A) ≅ B` is quasidiagonal, so `R = R_qd(E) ⊆ K⊗A`, and
`R = K⊗J_R` for an ideal `J_R` of `A`.
- For `K⊗J ⊆ R`, the quotient `E/(K⊗J)` is an extension of `B` by `K⊗(A/J)`,
  both UCT, so it is UCT.
- A full projection `p` of `J_R` gives the full projection `e_11 ⊗ p` of `R`.
- The radical theorem gives `R = 0`.

The K_0-embedding property follows from BD Proposition 4.6.
